name: Street Visual Quality in Beijing and Shanghai (Which Place Looks Better?)
description:
Method replication: same task, scale and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (122 Baidu street views re-fetched across central Beijing, inside the Fifth Ring Road, and central Shanghai, inside the Outer Ring Road, 2016 or later; one of four directions per point, 90° field of view, as in the paper's four-direction sampling).

Original study: Wang, Huang & Ye (2024), Buildings 14(11), 3332. Street quality in Beijing and Shanghai was measured in three dimensions. For visual perception, 10 experts who knew both cities answered 2,200 pairwise questions in a Java program, "Which place looks better?", on representative Baidu street views; Elo ratings trained a neural network on eight design elements (motorization, greenery, pedestrian space, sky view, building frontage, transparency, diversity, facilities), combined by AHP with accessibility and function scores.

Differences from the original study: (1) 122 new images instead of the paper's representative set; each participant compares 40 random pairs instead of the experts' 2,200 shared questions. (2) Anyone can take part; background and familiarity with each city are asked at the end. (3) The accessibility and function dimensions and the AHP weighting are not part of the survey.
author: Wang, Huang & Ye
